$comment: caique's capability matrix against the two packages it replaces (compat-oracle's LAYERS). Rendered by <CapabilityMatrix pkg="caique" /> from apps/docs-chassis and held by scripts/capabilities-lock.test.ts: every `ours` yes/partial names a test file and a title substring it contains, or a compat-oracle grade. LAYERS names inquirer and clack; the columns are what compat-oracle grades for them, @inquirer/core (inquirer-core, the loop every inquirer prompt runs on — the legacy inquirer package ships no tests to grade) and @clack/prompts. Neither is installed in this repository, so their cells cite the graded versions by URL — @inquirer/core 12.0.3, and @clack/core 1.5.1 under @clack/prompts 1.8.1 — or their vendored suites. `n/a` means the row does not apply, and says why. A row that could not be proved for every column is not here.

rows.capability: No terminal and no value is a refusal, not a wait
rows.why: `decide()` rules on every prompt before anything is drawn, and with nobody on stdin a missing value is a usage error rather than a prompt waiting for a person who is not there.

ours.title: never prompts without a terminal — the one that would be a bug report

inquirer-core.note: reads whatever input stream it is given; nothing checks whether a person is on it

clack.note: a prompt reads its input stream whether or not it is a terminal; only raw mode is conditional

rows.capability: The refusal names the flag to pass
rows.why: A prompt is bound to a flag, so the error says `--name is required when there is no terminal` and how to answer it, which an agent can act on.

ours.title: with no terminal, a missing required value is a usage error that names the flag

inquirer-core.note: a prompt has no flag behind it to name

clack.note: a prompt has no flag behind it to name

rows.capability: An agent on a terminal is refused, not prompted
rows.why: Under `CLAUDECODE`, `CURSOR_AGENT`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `GEMINI_CLI` or `AI_AGENT` there is a terminal and no person, so `decide()` asks roundel's `interactive()` and refuses, naming the flag, where asking only whether stdin is a terminal would wait forever.

ours.title: refuses under %s even on a terminal

inquirer-core.note: reads no agent variable; a prompt on a terminal waits for keys

clack.note: reads no agent variable; a prompt on a terminal waits for keys

rows.why: Under `--json`, or with `CI` set, a missing value is refused even on a terminal, because a machine is reading and nobody is there to type.

ours.title: never prompts under --json, and never under CI

inquirer-core.note: reads no CI variable and knows no --json

clack.note: reads CI to stop its spinner and progress animating, not to stop a prompt

themes.theme: The terminal as it was found

rows.capability: Raw mode is turned off only if the prompt turned it on
rows.why: A program that already had its terminal in raw mode keeps it when a prompt ends, and a signal mid-prompt still turns off the raw mode the prompt did turn on, through closeout.

ours.title: leaves raw mode on for a caller that already had it

inquirer-core.note: runs on node:readline with terminal: true, whose close() turns raw mode off whatever it was before

rows.capability: Custom prompt kinds through a validated plugin registry
rows.why: A widget for a kind outside the six built-ins is registered by name, and one without a static projection is refused with the code flagstaff and paratext use.

ours.title: a widget without `static` is E_NO_STATIC_PROJECTION, the same code flagstaff uses (R5)

inquirer-core.missing: a custom prompt is a function built with createPrompt; there is no registry, and nothing asks it for a text form

clack.missing: a custom prompt subclasses Prompt; there is no registry, and nothing asks it for a text form

rows.capability: A checker for widget plugins before they ship
rows.why: `npx caique check ./rating.mjs` validates a plugin against the family schema and exits 1 with a code and a fix when it is refused.

ours.title: refuses a malformed plugin with a code and a fix

inquirer-core.note: takes no plugins, so has nothing to check

clack.note: takes no plugins, so has nothing to check

rows.capability: Every runtime dependency from the same repository
rows.why: Installing it adds closeout, linegauge and paratext, released from this repository through one pipeline, and nothing else.

ours.title: installs nothing from outside this repository — dependencies, peers or optional (D-111)

inquirer-core.note: seven dependencies, among them signal-exit, mute-stream and cli-width

rows.why: `caique/inquirer` — `createPrompt`, the hooks and the keypress helpers — is graded by @inquirer/core 12.0.3's own tests, unedited, rendered through a headless terminal.

inquirer-core.note: its own suite, the control run

rows.why: `caique/clack` is graded by the behavioural cases of @clack/prompts 1.8.1's own suite, with the snapshots of clack's exact frames subtracted by name, and one case that grades @clack/core's module state rather than @clack/prompts (D-20260930-caique-clack-core-exclusion).

clack.note: its own suite, the control run
